chapter_summary: Jesus prepares His disciples for persecution, sorrow, and His departure. He promises the Spirit of truth, teaches about prayer and the Father’s love, predicts the disciples’ scattering, and promises peace amid trouble.
main_lesson: Jesus tells the truth about sorrow and trouble while preparing His disciples to trust His victory. The personal Spirit will testify about Jesus and guide the apostles, and the Father welcomes prayer through the Son.

memory_verse.kjv: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
memory_verse.little_bible: I have spoken these things to you so that in me you may have peace. In the world you will have trouble; but be cheerful. I have overcome the world.”

parent_guide: Access: default for ages 6–8 and 9–12 with adult context; ages 3–5 receive only carefully curated verses such as 6–7, 12, 20, 22, 27–28, and 33. Sensitivity: religious exclusion, killing and persecution, grief, death, abandonment, childbirth and varied family histories, guilt and conviction, spiritual conflict, prayer expectations, fear, and complex Trinitarian teaching. Historical persecution must never be generalized against Jewish people or used to encourage silent endurance; children should report threats, bullying, or harm immediately. The Spirit is a personal divine agent whose witness centers Jesus, not a private voice children must obey. Conviction is not shame or coerced disclosure. Birth imagery should remain non-graphic and optional. Prayer is not guaranteed wish fulfillment. The disciples’ scattering never normalizes child abandonment. Jesus’ peace permits grief and fear and never requires remaining in danger.
application_for_children: Children may ask honest questions, name grief or fear, pause difficult content, pray while trusting God with outcomes, and seek safe help whenever harm or abandonment occurs. They can learn that Jesus has overcome the world without pretending trouble is unreal.

verses.kjv: These things have I spoken unto you, that ye should not be offended.
verses.little_bible: I have spoken these things to you so that you should not stumble.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus prepared them so they would not stumble.
verses.meaning: Jesus prepares the disciples for coming pressure so it will not destroy their faith. Preparation supports resilience, not fear.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can knowing about a hard event help someone prepare safely?
verses.family_discussion: Make a calm plan for one difficult event your family can reasonably prepare for.
verses.do_it_today: Optionally make a small preparation checklist.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:1, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service.
verses.little_bible: They will put you out of the synagogues. Yes, the time is coming when whoever kills you will think that he is offering service to God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus warned that people would expel and even kill disciples while claiming to serve God.
verses.meaning: This historical warning concerns expulsion from Jewish communal worship and lethal persecution of Jesus’ followers. It must not be generalized against Jewish people or used to tell children to endure threats silently; danger requires immediate safe-adult help.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What should someone do if threatened for their beliefs? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Review trusted adults and emergency help; no personal disclosure is required.
verses.do_it_today: With an adult, write two safe-help contacts, or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:2, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: And these things will they do unto you, because they have not known the Father, nor me.
verses.little_bible: And these things will they do to you, because they have not known the Father, nor me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They would do this because they did not know the Father or Jesus.
verses.meaning: Persecutors’ zeal rests on not truly knowing the Father or Jesus. Religious language does not make violence holy.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why does religious language never make violence right?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss why violence in God’s name contradicts Jesus’ teaching.
verses.do_it_today: Say together, “Violence does not become holy by using God’s name.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:3, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: But these things have I told you, that when the time shall come, ye may remember that I told you of them. And these things I said not unto you at the beginning, because I was with you.
verses.little_bible: But I have told you these things so that when the time comes, you may remember that I told you about them. I did not say these things to you at the beginning, because I was with you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus warned them now so they would remember later.
verses.meaning: Jesus’ advance warning will help the disciples interpret events after his departure. He had shielded them through his physical presence earlier.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can a warning help without creating panic?
verses.family_discussion: Talk about warnings that are clear, proportionate, and hopeful.
verses.do_it_today: Draw a warning sign beside a safe path forward.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:4, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: But now I go my way to him that sent me; and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou?
verses.little_bible: But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, “Where are you going?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus was returning to the one who sent him, but none of the disciples asked where he was going.
verses.meaning: Jesus returns to the Father who sent him and notes that grief has narrowed the disciples’ attention. Their earlier questions do not cancel this immediate observation.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How might grief make questions harder to ask?
verses.family_discussion: Name how grief can affect attention without blaming the grieving person.
verses.do_it_today: Pause and name a feeling, or choose not to.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:5, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: But because I have said these things unto you, sorrow hath filled your heart.
verses.little_bible: But because I have said these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciples’ hearts were full of sorrow.
verses.meaning: Sorrow is a valid response to anticipated separation. Jesus names it without shame or demanding cheerfulness.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What can a caring person do when sorrow fills someone’s heart?
verses.family_discussion: Offer quiet company; nobody must explain private sadness.
verses.do_it_today: Offer someone quiet company without asking for details.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:6, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.
verses.little_bible: Nevertheless I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Comforter will not come to you; but if I depart, I will send him to you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said his leaving would allow the Comforter to come.
verses.meaning: Jesus says his departure is necessary for the Comforter’s mission. The Spirit is a personal divine agent, not a feeling, force, private voice, or imaginary companion.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse say the Spirit does after Jesus leaves?
verses.family_discussion: Compare a person who relates and speaks with an impersonal force.
verses.do_it_today: Write three actions the verse gives the Spirit.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:7, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:
verses.little_bible: And when he comes, he will show the world that it is wrong about sin, righteousness, and judgment:
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Comforter would expose truth about sin, righteousness, and judgment.
verses.meaning: The Spirit exposes the world’s mistaken verdicts concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment. Conviction tells truth and leads toward Christ; it is not humiliation, coerced confession, or pressure to disclose secrets to an app.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How is truthful conviction different from shame? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Practise truthful correction that protects dignity and never demands secrets.
verses.do_it_today: Practise: “That was wrong, but you are not worthless.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:8, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Of sin, because they believe not on me;
verses.little_bible: concerning sin, because they do not believe in me;
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Sin was exposed because people did not believe in Jesus.
verses.meaning: At the heart of the world’s sin is rejection of Jesus. This does not mean every question or developmental uncertainty is malicious unbelief.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why are honest questions different from rejecting Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Welcome one honest question without labeling the questioner.
verses.do_it_today: Ask one honest question, or simply listen.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:9, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;
verses.little_bible: Concerning righteousness, because I go to my Father, and you will no longer see me;
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus’ return to the Father would show righteousness.
verses.meaning: Jesus connects righteousness with his return to the Father and disappearance from the disciples’ sight. Many Christians understand this as the Father’s vindication of Jesus despite the world’s verdict; other readings emphasize the exposure of the world’s false righteousness or the righteousness Jesus provides. It never means children become morally perfect.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus’ return to the Father reveal?
verses.family_discussion: Trace how departure to the Father changes the world’s verdict on Jesus.
verses.do_it_today: Draw an arrow showing Jesus returning to the Father.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:10, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.
verses.little_bible: Concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The world’s ruler had already been judged.
verses.meaning: Satan, the ruler of this world, stands judged through Jesus’ victory. Satan is created and limited, never God’s equal; avoid frightening imagery.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why is evil never equal to God?
verses.family_discussion: Reassure younger listeners that God is not locked in a battle between equals.
verses.do_it_today: Say, “God is greater than evil,” or listen.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:11, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.
verses.little_bible: I have yet many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus had more to say than they could bear then.
verses.meaning: Jesus respects the disciples’ present capacity and does not overload them. Adults should likewise pace difficult teaching and permit children to pause.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus’ pacing teach adults and learners?
verses.family_discussion: Choose a stop signal any child can use during hard content.
verses.do_it_today: Use a stop card during one difficult reading.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:12, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.
verses.little_bible: However, when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all truth. For he will not speak from himself, but whatever he hears, he will speak; and he will show you things to come.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Spirit of truth would guide them, speak what he heard, and tell them what was coming.
verses.meaning: The personal Spirit faithfully communicates within the divine mission, guides the apostles into the truth needed for their witness, and declares things to come. This apostolic promise does not give every believer all knowledge, guaranteed predictions, infallible private impressions, audible commands, or additions equal to Scripture.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can we test a claimed spiritual message safely?
verses.family_discussion: Test impressions by Scripture and wise trusted adults. Reject and report any message that asks for harm, secrecy, isolation, or unsafe behaviour.
verses.do_it_today: Check one claim against a Gospel passage with an adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:13, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you.
verses.little_bible: He will glorify me, for he will receive what is mine and show it to you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Spirit would glorify Jesus and show his truth to them.
verses.meaning: The Spirit’s ministry centers and glorifies Jesus rather than the messenger or a sensational experience.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Whom does the Spirit glorify?
verses.family_discussion: Notice whether teaching points toward Jesus or toward the speaker’s importance.
verses.do_it_today: Circle every reference to Jesus in the verse.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:14, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: All things that the Father hath are mine: therefore said I, that he shall take of mine, and shall shew it unto you.
verses.little_bible: Everything the Father has is mine. Therefore I said that he will take what is mine and show it to you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: All the Father has belongs to Jesus; the Spirit would show it.
verses.meaning: Father, Son, and Spirit act distinctly yet in perfect unity. The verse supports Trinitarian reflection without collapsing them into one person.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How are Father, Son, and Spirit distinct in this verse?
verses.family_discussion: List distinct actions of Father, Son, and Spirit without pretending to solve every mystery.
verses.do_it_today: Use three different colours for Father, Son, and Spirit.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:15, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me, because I go to the Father.
verses.little_bible: A little while, and you will not see me: and again, a little while, and you will see me, because I go to the Father.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Soon they would not see Jesus, then they would see him.
verses.meaning: Jesus speaks of his imminent death and subsequent resurrection appearances in deliberately compressed language; some traditions also hear wider departure-and-return themes.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What events might Jesus mean by not seeing and seeing again?
verses.family_discussion: Place death, resurrection, and return-to-Father cards in order.
verses.do_it_today: Put three story cards in order with an adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:16, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Then said some of his disciples among themselves, What is this that he saith unto us, A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me: and, Because I go to the Father?
verses.little_bible: Then some of his disciples said among themselves, “What is this that he says to us, ‘A little while, and you will not see me; and again, a little while, and you will see me,’ and, ‘Because I am going to the Father’?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciples wondered what Jesus meant.
verses.meaning: The disciples openly discuss confusing words. Their uncertainty models honest collaborative learning.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What is helpful about discussing confusion together?
verses.family_discussion: Let everyone contribute a question or pass.
verses.do_it_today: Add one question to a family question jar.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:17, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: They said therefore, What is this that he saith, A little while? we cannot tell what he saith.
verses.little_bible: Therefore they said, “What is this that he says, ‘A little while’? We do not know what he says.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They said, “We do not understand ‘a little while.’”
verses.meaning: Repetition shows genuine confusion, not stubbornness. Children may say they do not understand without spiritual blame.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What words can you use when you do not understand?
verses.family_discussion: Practise saying, “Please explain that another way.”
verses.do_it_today: Use the words, “I do not understand yet.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:18, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Now Jesus knew that they were desirous to ask him, and said unto them, Do ye enquire among yourselves of that I said, A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me?
verses.little_bible: Now Jesus knew that they wanted to ask him, and said to them, ‘Are you asking among yourselves about what I said: “A little while, and you will not see me; and again, a little while, and you will see me”?’
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus knew their unspoken question.
verses.meaning: Jesus knows their question but still engages it rather than shaming them. The app must never claim Jesus-like access to a child’s hidden thoughts.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why might Jesus let them ask even though he knows?
verses.family_discussion: Model listening even when you think you know the question.
verses.do_it_today: Invite a question without guessing someone’s private thoughts.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:19, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.
verses.little_bible: Truly, truly, I say to you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice: and you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciples would weep while the world rejoiced. Their sorrow would turn into joy.
verses.meaning: Jesus predicts real grief at his death and joy following his resurrection. Christian joy does not forbid mourning, tears, or help-seeking.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can sorrow and future joy both be true? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Make room for grief without rushing toward a happy ending.
verses.do_it_today: Hold space for sadness without fixing it.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:20, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow, because her hour is come: but as soon as she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for joy that a man is born into the world.
verses.little_bible: A woman has sorrow when she is in labor, because her time has come. But as soon as she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers the pain, because of her joy that a person has been born into the world.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus compared sorrow followed by joy to labour followed by a child’s birth.
verses.meaning: The childbirth image moves from intense labour to joy after birth. Keep it non-graphic and sensitive to infertility, loss, adoption, foster care, and varied birth-family experiences; no child must discuss personal family history. This is not a promise that every birth ends safely or that joy erases pain, trauma, loss, or grief.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can families discuss this image gently? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Acknowledge different family stories and allow everyone to pass.
verses.do_it_today: Skip the birth image if it touches family pain.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:21, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
verses.little_bible: And you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus would see them again, bringing lasting joy.
verses.meaning: Resurrection reunion will transform the disciples’ sorrow into joy that opponents cannot remove. This does not promise uninterrupted happiness or deny later hardship.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why does lasting joy not mean constant happiness?
verses.family_discussion: Name ordinary joy that can coexist with ongoing difficulty.
verses.do_it_today: Draw joy as a light that remains during rain.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:22, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: And in that day ye shall ask me nothing. Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you.
verses.little_bible: And on that day you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly, I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give it to you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: In that day they would ask Jesus no more questions. They could ask the Father in Jesus’ name.
verses.meaning: Prayer in Jesus’ name rests on access to the Father through him. “Whatever” remains shaped by Jesus’ teaching and mission, not guaranteed wishes.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How should Jesus’ teaching shape prayer requests?
verses.family_discussion: Rewrite one request to include trust in Jesus’ wisdom and will.
verses.do_it_today: If you wish, pray while leaving the outcome with God. You may pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:23, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Hitherto have ye asked nothing in my name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be full.
verses.little_bible: Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be full.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus told them to ask in his name so their joy would be full.
verses.meaning: Jesus invites dependent prayer and promises reception and full joy in context. Prayer is not magic, and unanswered or differently answered prayer is not proof of weak faith.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What can someone remember when prayer is answered differently?
verses.family_discussion: Share a non-shaming way to support someone after disappointment.
verses.do_it_today: After prayer, choose one safe next step you can take.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:24, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: These things have I spoken unto you in proverbs: but the time cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in proverbs, but I shall shew you plainly of the Father.
verses.little_bible: I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. But the time is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus would soon speak plainly about the Father.
verses.meaning: Jesus contrasts figurative teaching with forthcoming clarity about the Father. Figurative language is not deceit; it can prepare learners for truth.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why might a teacher sometimes use a picture or figure?
verses.family_discussion: Choose a familiar metaphor and explain both its help and its limits.
verses.do_it_today: Explain one gentle picture used by Jesus.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:25, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: At that day ye shall ask in my name: and I say not unto you, that I will pray the Father for you:
verses.little_bible: On that day you will ask in my name. I do not say to you that I will ask the Father for you,
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They would ask in Jesus’ name. Jesus said he was not saying that he would ask the Father for them.
verses.meaning: The disciples will approach the Father in Jesus’ name. Jesus is not saying his mediation is unnecessary, but emphasizing the Father’s direct welcome.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What does direct access to the Father communicate?
verses.family_discussion: Thank God together for welcoming prayer through Jesus.
verses.do_it_today: If you wish, address a short prayer to the Father through Jesus. You may pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:26, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: For the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, and have believed that I came out from God.
verses.little_bible: For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me, and have believed that I came from God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Father loved them because they loved Jesus and believed he came from God.
verses.meaning: The Father’s love is personally directed toward the disciples who love and trust the Son. Their love is response within grace, not payment that earns affection.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why is love not something disciples purchase?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss grace as the beginning of response, not a wage for belief.
verses.do_it_today: Receive love today without making an achievement list.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:27, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: I came forth from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go to the Father.
verses.little_bible: I came from the Father and have come into the world. Again, I leave the world and go to the Father.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus came from the Father and was returning to him.
verses.meaning: Jesus summarizes his mission: from the Father into the world and back to the Father through death, resurrection, and ascension.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What journey does Jesus summarize?
verses.family_discussion: Map Jesus’ movement from Father, to world, and back to Father.
verses.do_it_today: Trace Jesus’ journey with arrows.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:28, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: His disciples said unto him, Lo, now speakest thou plainly, and speakest no proverb.
verses.little_bible: His disciples said to him, “Look, now you speak plainly and use no figure.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciples said Jesus was now speaking plainly.
verses.meaning: The disciples believe the teaching is now direct. Their confidence will soon be tested, showing that verbal clarity does not equal complete readiness.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Can understanding words and being ready differ?
verses.family_discussion: Remember a time practice was needed after instructions became clear.
verses.do_it_today: Practise one instruction after hearing it clearly.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:29, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Now are we sure that thou knowest all things, and needest not that any man should ask thee: by this we believe that thou camest forth from God.
verses.little_bible: Now we are sure that you know all things and do not need anyone to ask you. By this we believe that you came from God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciples said Jesus knew everything without needing their questions. Because of this, they believed he came from God.
verses.meaning: They confess Jesus’ knowledge and divine origin. Their faith is genuine but not yet as strong as they suppose.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What did the disciples believe about Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Distinguish sincere confession from overconfidence.
verses.do_it_today: Retell one true claim the disciples made.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:30, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Jesus answered them, Do ye now believe?
verses.little_bible: Jesus answered them, “Do you now believe?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus asked, “Do you believe now?”
verses.meaning: Jesus’ question gently tests the confidence of their declaration in light of the scattering he is about to predict.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why might Jesus question confident faith?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss how questions can strengthen rather than mock faith.
verses.do_it_today: If you wish, add, ‘Jesus, strengthen our faith,’ to a confident statement. You may pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:31, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Behold, the hour cometh, yea, is now come, that ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
verses.little_bible: Behold, the hour is coming—yes, has now come—when you will be scattered, each one to his own place, and will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They would scatter and leave Jesus, but the Father remained with him.
verses.meaning: The disciples will abandon Jesus during his arrest, yet the Father remains with him. This is not a template for child abandonment or a claim that human care is unnecessary; children left alone must seek safe help.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Where can a child seek help when people leave? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Repeat: abandonment in this story never makes abandoning a child acceptable.
verses.do_it_today: Name a safe adult or support number, or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 16:32, Jesus teaching attentive disciples in an upper room, historically appropriate, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
verses.little_bible: I have spoken these things to you so that in me you might have peace. In the world you will have trouble; but take courage. I have overcome the world.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus promised peace in himself amid trouble because he overcame the world.
verses.meaning: Jesus promises peace located in relationship with him while honestly acknowledging trouble. Courage rests on his victory, not denial, emotional suppression, staying in danger, or pretending harm is acceptable.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive this teaching with truth, wisdom, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can peace, trouble, courage, and reporting harm coexist?
verses.family_discussion: Create a sentence: “We can seek peace and still leave danger.”
verses.do_it_today: Choose a calming action and remember to report danger.
